children: According to CNBC, Microsoft shares fell nearly 9% over the two weeks after reaching an all-time closing high on Nov. 4, the day after the midterm elections, as an Outlook outage hit during a rough week of technology disruptions. Microsoft was the first major company affected in a string of outages that disrupted corporate communications, airline operations and banking transactions. Since the company’s late-July earnings report, its stock had climbed 30%. Its Oct. 28 earnings showed Azure revenue rose 48% to $33.2 billion. At its Ignite conference Tuesday, Microsoft presented Copilot as a central hub for workplace productivity.

title: Microsoft Shares Pull Back 9% From Record High After Election and Outlook Outage
